title: Composition adds the bounds on differential order
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $C$ an $R$-algebra with structure map $R\to C$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and let $L,M,N$ be $C$-modules, regarded as $R$-modules by restriction of scalars. For a nonnegative integer $n$, an $R$-linear map $T$ between $C$-modules has differential order at most $0$ when it is $C$-linear, and recursively has differential order at most $n>0$ when, for every $c\in C$, the map $[T,c]:x\mapsto T(cx)-cT(x)$ has differential order at most $n-1$. Let $k,l\geq0$. If $D:L\to M$ and $E:M\to N$ are $R$-linear maps of differential orders at most $k$ and $l$, respectively, then $E\circ D:L\to N$ has differential order at most $k+l$.

source.place: Tag 09CJ, lemma-composition-differential-operators; recursive definition is Tag 09CI, definition-differential-operators.

proof.text: Write $\delta_c(T)(x)=T(cx)-cT(x)$. Multiplication by $c$ on any $C$-module is $R$-linear, since the $R$-action is through the commutative ring $C$; hence every $\delta_c(T)$ is $R$-linear. For each $n$, the zero map has order at most $n$, and sums of maps of order at most $n$ have order at most $n$: at $n=0$ this is closure of $C$-linear maps under zero and addition; at $n>0$ use $\delta_c(0)=0$ and $\delta_c(T+U)=\delta_c(T)+\delta_c(U)$ and induction on $n$. These are direct consequences of the recursive definition in the statement.

source.place: Tag 09CJ, lemma-composition-differential-operators, proof; Tag 09CI, definition-differential-operators and the immediately following paragraph.

proof.text: Prove the composition assertion by strong induction on $s=k+l$, for every pair of nonnegative bounds and every triple of $C$-modules. If $s=0$, then $k=l=0$ and $E\circ D$ is $C$-linear: $(E\circ D)(cx)=E(cD(x))=cE(D(x))$. Thus it has order at most $0$. For $s>0$, assume the assertion for every strictly smaller sum.

source.place: Tag 09CJ, lemma-composition-differential-operators, proof; Tag 09CI, definition-differential-operators and the immediately following paragraph.

proof.text: Fix $c\in C$. Additivity of $E$ gives, for each $x\in L$, $$\delta_c(E\circ D)(x)=E(D(cx))-cE(D(x))=E(D(cx)-cD(x))+(E(cD(x))-cE(D(x))).$$ Therefore $$\delta_c(E\circ D)=E\circ\delta_c(D)+\delta_c(E)\circ D.$$ The two summands are maps from $L$ to $N$, so their sum is defined.

source.place: Tag 09CJ, lemma-composition-differential-operators, proof; Tag 09CI, definition-differential-operators and the immediately following paragraph.

proof.text: If $k>0$, the recursive definition gives order at most $k-1$ for $\delta_c(D)$, and the induction hypothesis applied to the bounds $(k-1,l)$ gives order at most $s-1$ for $E\circ\delta_c(D)$. If $k=0$, then $D$ is $C$-linear, so this summand is zero and has order at most $s-1$ by step 1. Similarly, if $l>0$, apply the induction hypothesis to $(k,l-1)$ to bound $\delta_c(E)\circ D$ by $s-1$; if $l=0$, that summand is zero. Step 1 now shows that their sum has order at most $s-1$. This holds for every $c\in C$. Since $E\circ D$ is $R$-linear, the recursive definition proves it has order at most $s=k+l$.
